# ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops Daily Update (Feb 2, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today's development focused on enhancing betanet functionality with new RevShare tasks and improving task submission guidelines. Discussions on active issues covered `op-supernode` safe label adjustments and `Flashblocks` support in Geth.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

### Betanet RevShare Functionality
Two new betanet tasks were added for Sepolia to upgrade and configure RevShare functionality for the `revshare-beta-1` chain, updating it to U18. The status of these tasks was also updated. ([#1365](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1365), [#1366](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1366))

### Task Submission Process Improvements
Improvements were made to the task submission process by updating the `NEW_TASK_GUIDE.md` to include a "Before Submitting Your Task for Review" section, requiring task authors to follow best practices and simulation requirements. ([#1357](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1357))

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
No new pull requests were opened today.

## CLOSED ISSUES
No issues were closed today.

## NEW ISSUES
No new issues were reported today.

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### `op-supernode`: Safe Label Adjusting
Discussion continued on how `op-supernode` should manage the `Safe` label in the Execution Layer (EL) and Consensus Layer (CL). A key point raised is the danger of multiple stateful controllers updating the same engine, leading to potential desynchronization. The current leaning is for the CL to maintain the full set of pointers [U,S,C,F] and remain the sole controller of the engine, with the supernode controlling the EL via the virtual node/CL. This approach addresses concerns about managing RPC responses from virtual nodes, allowing them to return rich sync status. ([#18976](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/18976))

### Flashblocks Support within Geth
The conversation around integrating `Flashblocks` support into `op-geth` saw an update, with a link provided to the `op-geth` version that includes Firehose Live Tracer and Flashblock(s) support. The importance of merging this functionality into `op-geth` was highlighted, as running archive versions of Reth currently consumes significant disk space and is less straightforward than Geth. ([#756](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/756))

### `BlockNotFoundError` in Step 5 (Prove the withdrawal on L1)
Further analysis of the `BlockNotFoundError` in the ETH bridge tutorial revealed that the Optimism SDK includes a validation step for the output root, which appears to be missing in Viem's `Withdrawals guide` and related actions. This omission can lead to issues when a withdrawal is initiated on L2 and `waitToProve` is executed immediately, as the state root might not yet be published to L1. A temporary workaround involving manual retrieval and overriding of output root data was suggested. ([#1956](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/1956))
